hints: A polynomial update adds a sequence 1,2,3,... across its target interval.
Represent the update as a linear function of position: at index i, add i-start+1.
Use a lazy segment tree storing sum and pending linear coefficients.
analogy: A ramp can be described by a slope plus a starting offset, so its total over a segment is computed from index sums.
example: Adding 1,2,3 to positions 4,5,6 increases their total by 6.
correctness: The linear expression gives the exact added value at every position; summing it over a segment and composing tags preserves all past updates.
complexity: O(log n) per update/query and O(n) space.
algorithm: For an update [a,b], position i receives i-a+1. Store pending additions as slope and offset, so a segment's added sum is slope*sum(indices)+offset*length. Push adjusted coefficients to children; query sums from the segment tree.
